correctness.rationale: For x in (0,1), y in [0,1], write s=1-x, t=1-xy, b=gamma*s/x, q=gamma+(1-gamma)x. The mixed derivative is D1+D2 with D1=s^b(s-q-gamma*s*log(s)/x), D2=t^b[gamma+2(1-gamma)x+(gamma*q/x)*(-log(t)-s*(1-t)/t)]. Since (-log(t)-s*(1-t)/t) decreases from a nonnegative value to zero on t in [s,1], for 0<=gamma<=1 one obtains c>=s^b[1-gamma*x-gamma*s*log(s)/x]>0. Boundary and margin limits are exact. For gamma>1, c(x,0)->1-gamma<0 as x->1; for gamma<0, c(x,y)->1-gamma-gamma*log(1-y), which is negative for y sufficiently close to one. A strictly increasing h_a(u)=u^a(-log u)/(1-u) for a>=1 proves strict parameter order. The full analytic proof is in RESULT.md. A reproducible 60-digit checker passed 3614 finite supporting checks; finite tests are not the basis of the theorem.

value.rationale: The source expressly says the Int1 copula is parameter-free and suffers from lack of flexibility, while suggesting parameter additions without developing them. This exact, natural exponent interpolation bridges independence and Int1; the proof determines both sharp forbidden parameter sides rather than imposing a conservative sufficient interval. Strict pointwise concordance ordering makes the parameter interpretable as dependence strength and ensures continuously varying Spearman association. The finite difference power formula is not an affine endpoint mixture. This gives a complete, motivated new model class; no empirical superiority is inferred.
